papers_and_evidence.article_title: Wireless Cyber-Physical Systems Performance Evaluation through a Graph Database Approach
papers_and_evidence.locators: Data Collection; graph data model; Results (Figs. 6, 8–14). NCBI BioC passage offsets 22218, 36183, 41919, 47205, 49933, 51421 and 52777.
papers_and_evidence.results: In the published comparison each run emulated 20 parts in about 12 minutes of network activity. Four communication conditions were compared. A roughly 120 ms robot program scan led to longer network transactions being offset by shorter waits for the next eligible controller update in the studied cases. No separate per-row clock synchronization error or independent physical-motion onset was recovered here. No raw measurement counts or sensor-sample AoI are inferred.

papers_and_evidence.locator: NIST author copy, workcell and graph methods, Fig. 6. The data release explicitly refers to this conference paper.
Workcell Description; Process Monitoring and Diagnostics. The related but distinct NIST process dataset should not be used to augment counts for the wireless graph trials.
